Take a 15-minute walk together. Each of you names one thing you're thankful for.
Pray together before bed one night. Let your kid pray first.
Veterans Day week: make a thank-you card together and give it to a veteran.
Build something together: a fort, a model, or a Lego build. Let them lead.
Make a gratitude list together and post it on the fridge.
Cook one meal together. They pick the dish.
Memorize Proverbs 27:17 together and say it at dinner.
Do 20 push-ups together, any style. Count out loud.
Read the Christmas story together in Luke 2.
Look back at the year together: name three things God did for your family.
Pray together for the year ahead and write one goal each.
Write a note to Mom together and hide it where she'll find it.
Serve a neighbor together: rake leaves, take out bins, or bring a treat.
Read one chapter of a Gospel together and ask what Jesus did.
Play catch or shoot hoops for 20 minutes with no phones.
Give each kid one job to do with you this week, and do it side by side.
Have a 10-minute talk: ask what's been hard this week, then just listen.
Go outside at night and look at the stars. Read Psalm 19:1 together.
Race each other: sprint, crawl or hop. Laugh more than you win.
Pick one family rule together and write it on the fridge.
Plank together. See who can hold it longest.
Read the Easter story together in Luke 24 and talk about why the empty tomb matters.
Take turns praying for each person in the family by name.
Fix or clean something in the house together.
Let your kid teach you something they're good at.
Go on a hike or long walk and pray at the halfway point.
Give away a toy, book or clothes together to someone who needs it.
Write down three things you love about each other.
Do a family workout: 3 rounds of 10 squats, 10 jumping jacks and a 20-second plank.
Ask Grandma or Grandpa a question about their faith together.
Wash the car or bikes together.
Memorial Day week: visit a memorial or flag and pray for families who lost someone.
Memorize Joshua 1:9 together.
Plan a family movie or game night and let them choose.
Bake something and deliver it to a friend.
Go to bed early one night and read together instead of screens.
Plant something together and water it each day this week.
Bike ride or scooter together around the neighborhood.
Tell your kid a story about a time God helped you.
Make breakfast for Mom together.
Do 50 jumping jacks together every day for 3 days.
Draw or write what you each want to be known for.
Pray over a meal together and let your kid lead it.
Throw, kick or hit a ball together for 20 minutes.
Clean your kid's room together. Work, then celebrate.
Write a letter to a missionary or a soldier together.
Read Psalm 23 together and talk about what a shepherd does.
Learn one new skill together: tie a knot, change a tire or check the oil.
Do a no-screens hour together. Play a board or card game.
Ask your kid how you can pray for them, then pray right then.
Walk the dog or take a walk and pick up trash along the way.
Do wall sits together. Talk until one of you quits.
